policies.name: Corporate Password Reset & Self-Service Portal
policies.problemDescription: User has forgotten their domain password, password has expired, or user is unable to authenticate due to credential mismatch.
policies.approvedSolution: Direct user to the Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) portal or perform an out-of-band verified identity reset via the IT Helpdesk console.
stepByStepInstructions: 1. Confirm user identity via two-factor mobile push or manager confirmation callback.
2. Direct user to https://sspr.internal.local or open Active Directory Users & Computers.
3. If performing manual reset: check 'User must change password at next logon' and generate a compliant temporary password (min 16 chars).
4. Instruct user to sign into workstation or portal using the temporary password.
5. Verify successful sign-in and confirm multi-factor authentication (MFA) token status.
6. Document the identity verification method in the ticket and close.

policies.name: Account Lockout & Brute-Force Remediation
policies.problemDescription: User account has been locked out after exceeding the maximum allowed consecutive failed logon attempts (5 attempts threshold).
policies.approvedSolution: Inspect the source domain controller for repeated bad password events, unlock the domain account, and clear cached credentials on secondary devices.
stepByStepInstructions: 1. Query the LockoutStatus diagnostic tool to identify which workstation or service caused the repeated bad password events.
2. Verify with the user if they recently changed their password on mobile, tablet, or secondary laptops.
3. Instruct the user to disconnect Wi-Fi on secondary devices temporarily to avoid re-locking.
4. In AD Users & Computers, right-click the user account, select Properties -> Account -> check 'Unlock account' -> click Apply.
5. Have user attempt login from their primary workstation.
6. Assist user in updating cached credentials on secondary devices before reconnecting network.
7. Resolve ticket and set category to Security: Account Lockout.

policies.name: Corporate Email & Mailbox Access Troubleshooting
policies.problemDescription: User cannot send, receive, or access emails in Microsoft Outlook or the webmail client, experiences mailbox quota errors, or sync errors.
policies.approvedSolution: Check Exchange Online tenant status, verify mailbox storage capacity, and repair corrupted local OST cache or Outlook mail profiles.
stepByStepInstructions: 1. Verify tenant-wide Exchange status at status.internal.local.
2. Check user's mailbox quota in Microsoft 365 Admin Center (ensure under 95% capacity).
3. Test webmail access via https://outlook.office.com to isolate desktop client versus server-side issues.
4. If webmail works, close Outlook on client machine and launch 'outlook.exe /safe'.
5. If error persists, navigate to Control Panel -> Mail -> Show Profiles and rebuild corrupted profile.
6. Confirm send/receive synchronization completes with 0 errors.
7. Close ticket and record resolution as Outlook Profile Rebuild.

policies.name: Local Network & Wi-Fi Connectivity Resolution
policies.problemDescription: Device cannot connect to the corporate wired LAN or wireless 802.1x network, receives self-assigned APIPA IP (169.254.x.x), or suffers frequent disconnects.
policies.approvedSolution: Renew DHCP lease, flush DNS cache, verify 802.1x machine certificate validity, and validate switch port status.
stepByStepInstructions: 1. Check physical link light on Ethernet adapter or confirm corporate SSID 'Corp-Secure-WiFi' is visible.
2. Open Command Prompt as Administrator and run 'ipconfig /release' followed by 'ipconfig /renew'.
3. Execute 'ipconfig /flushdns' and verify DNS server reaches 10.0.0.10 and 10.0.0.11.
4. Check computer certificates MMC (certlm.msc) to verify 'Corporate Device Root CA' is valid and not expired.
5. If on Wi-Fi, forget 'Corp-Secure-WiFi' network profile and rejoin using domain credentials.
6. If wired, test cable on an alternate verified wall jack.
7. Validate successful ping to internal default gateway and external public DNS (8.8.8.8).

policies.name: Software Installation & Application Packaging Approval
policies.problemDescription: User requests new software installation, software upgrade, license assignment, or installation error remediation for corporate workstations.
policies.approvedSolution: Deploy approved software via Intune Company Portal self-service catalog or submit manager-approved procurement request for uncataloged commercial software.
stepByStepInstructions: 1. Check if requested application is already in the Approved Software Catalog (Standard Tier).
2. Instruct user to open 'Company Portal' from Start Menu and click 'Install' on the approved app.
3. If application is non-standard or commercial: verify manager budget approval ticket.
4. Ensure security team review is logged for third-party executable packages.
5. Deploy via Intune device group or perform remote unattended MSI installation using deployment credentials.
6. Verify license allocation in IT Asset Management system.
7. Have user launch the application to verify launch without administrative prompts.

policies.name: Printer & Multifunction Peripheral Troubleshooting
policies.problemDescription: Printer offline, documents stuck in print queue, paper jams, toner replacement, or unable to map network print queue.
policies.approvedSolution: Restart local Print Spooler service, remove hung print jobs from spool directory, or remap the universal Follow-Me print queue.
stepByStepInstructions: 1. Verify printer hardware status (display screen, paper trays 1-3, toner levels).
2. On user machine, open 'services.msc' and locate 'Print Spooler'.
3. Stop the Print Spooler service.
4. Navigate to 'C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS' and delete all pending temporary spool files.
5. Start the Print Spooler service.
6. If printer is a network queue, remap via '\\printserver01\FollowMe-Global'.
7. Send a standard Windows test page and verify output.

policies.name: Virtual Private Network (VPN) Remote Access
policies.problemDescription: Remote user cannot establish VPN connection, receives gateway timeout, SSL handshake failure, or split-tunneling routing issues.
policies.approvedSolution: Verify user VPN group membership in Active Directory, validate client client version, and test connection across alternative gateway endpoints.
stepByStepInstructions: 1. Confirm user is assigned to AD security group 'VPN-Remote-Users-Global'.
2. Ensure user has an active public internet connection by testing access to standard web services.
3. Launch VPN Client and ensure gateway is set to 'vpn.company.com' (or failover 'vpn-backup.company.com').
4. Prompt user for standard corporate credentials followed by Duo/MFA Push approval.
5. If connection fails with TLS certificate warning, update client root certificates.
6. If route flapping occurs, disable IPv6 on the home Wi-Fi adapter.
7. Confirm IP assignment within 10.240.x.x pool and verify access to intranet resources.

policies.name: Access Permissions & Role-Based Security Group Request
policies.problemDescription: User receives 'Access Denied', 'Permission Denied', or lacks authorization to shared network folders, SharePoint document libraries, or Jira projects.
policies.approvedSolution: Obtain written approval from the departmental Data Owner, then add the user's AD object to the designated Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) security group.
stepByStepInstructions: 1. Identify the specific folder path (UNC path) or SharePoint URL requested.
2. Check the Access Matrix to identify the designated Data Owner / Department Manager.
3. Confirm written authorization or ticket approval from the Data Owner is attached.
4. In Active Directory / Azure AD, locate the target resource group (e.g., 'SG-Finance-ReadWrite').
5. Add user to the group with standard 90-day review flag.
6. Instruct user to lock (Win+L) and unlock their workstation to refresh Kerberos group membership tokens.
7. Confirm user can read/write to the requested resource.

policies.name: Hardware Malfunction & Physical Asset Diagnostic
policies.problemDescription: Physical workstation, laptop, monitor, docking station, battery, or peripheral is failing, crashing with blue screen (BSOD), or failing to power on.
policies.approvedSolution: Perform hardware diagnostics via OEM UEFI diagnostic tools, capture BSOD crash dump logs, or initiate hardware replacement / loaner laptop dispatch.
stepByStepInstructions: 1. If battery is swollen or physically hot, immediately instruct user to disconnect charger, power down, and move to fire-safe area.
2. For BSOD: reboot machine, tap F12 at boot, and run comprehensive OEM hardware diagnostics (ePSA / SupportAssist).
3. Review C:\Windows\Minidump files to identify faulted driver or failing hardware module (RAM/SSD).
4. For docking station issues: perform cold power cycle (unplug all cables, hold power 30s) and update Thunderbolt firmware.
5. If hardware diagnostic fails: record service tag, error code, and validation code.
6. Provision loaner laptop from IT depot and dispatch OEM warranty technician for on-site part replacement.
7. Update IT Asset Management CMDB inventory records with loaner and repair status.

policies.name: Data Recovery & File Restoration from Backup
policies.problemDescription: User accidentally deleted files, overwritten important documents, corrupted local directories, or suffered ransomware encryption.
policies.approvedSolution: Recover deleted items via OneDrive/SharePoint Version History, Previous Versions (VSS Shadow Copies), or Veeam Enterprise Backup archives.
stepByStepInstructions: 1. Collect exact filename, file path, and approximate date/time of last known good version.
2. Check user's local Windows Recycle Bin and Cloud Second-Stage Recycle Bin.
3. If stored on OneDrive/SharePoint: open file version history in browser and select 'Restore' on the desired timestamp.
4. If stored on enterprise file server: right-click parent folder -> Properties -> 'Previous Versions' tab to restore shadow copy snapshot.
5. If file was deleted beyond snapshot retention window: initiate restore job via enterprise Veeam Backup Console.
6. Restore file to a designated temporary recovery sandbox folder ('C:\IT_Recovery\Restored_Files') rather than overwriting in place.
7. Have user review and confirm integrity of the recovered file before closing ticket.
